slides.title: A controlled shift to November 19.
slides.subtitle: Protect the retail launch buffer. Keep the November 12 press embargo.
slides.notes: This is an internal draft for review. The recommendation does not authorize changing dates or sending external notices.

slides.title: Three dates. One clear sequence.
slides.subtitle: Packaging arrives before the press embargo and retail availability.
slides.notes: Packaging moved from November 4 to November 8. The extra week protects fulfilment. The press announcement should state the retail availability date clearly.

slides.title: What changes, what holds.
slides.subtitle: Keep the recommendation separate from actions that still need approval.
items: Retail availability moves seven days to November 19.
The press embargo remains November 12.
Paid media requires its own review after source access is restored.
slides.notes: The media buy tracker was excluded from this recommendation because its access expired. The dates use the permitted supplier ETA, retail calendar, and plan snapshot.

slides.title: Two approvals. Two boundaries.
slides.subtitle: A date decision never silently authorizes external delivery.
items: Jamie Davis approves or redirects the proposed retail date.
Four vendor notices are reviewed separately before sending.
Ops holds delivery until that specific action is approved.
slides.notes: These are proposed actions in a sample design. No notices were sent. Each approval should identify its actor, target, and exact content or change.

slides.title: The next step has an owner.
slides.subtitle: Keep progress visible without asking people to supervise every tool call.
items: Launch Planner maintains the plan and completion criteria.
Ops prepares vendor notices and holds delivery.
Jon T. restores and verifies access to the media source.
slides.notes: A question about presentation audience blocks only the briefing assignment. Date approval, source restoration, and message approval remain separate work.
